\title{Sasakian Manifolds}
\section{Definitions}
There are many equivalent definitons of Sasakian manifold.
We will take a viewpoint from [[PseuHerm|Pseudo-Hermitian Geometry]].

\begin{definition}
    A Sasakian manifold is a pseudo-Hermitian manifold $(M,H,J,\theta)$, whose pseudo-Hermitian torsion $\tau $  vanishes.
\end{definition}

The following proposition gives different characterizations of Sasakian manifolds. 

\begin{proposition}
   Let $(M^{2m+1},g)$ be a Riemannian manifold, $\nabla$ the Levi-Civita connection, and $R$ its curvature tensor.
  Then the following conditions are equivalent: 
   \begin{enumerate}
        \item $(M, g)$ is a Sasakian manifold.
        \item The associated cone manifold $(C(M), \tilde{g})= (M \times \rr^+,r^2g+dr^2)$ is a K\"ahler manifold. Therefore, Sasakian manifolds are the ``odd-dimensional'' generalization of K\"ahler manifolds.
        \item There exists a unit-length Killing vector field $T$ on $M$ such that the $(1,1)$-type tensor field $\Phi$ defined by $\Phi(X) = \nabla_X T$ satisfies
        \(
        (\nabla_X \Phi)(Y) = g(T, Y)X - g(X, Y)T , \quad \forall X,Y \in T(M).
        \)
        \item There exists a unit-length Killing vector field $T$ on $M$ such that the curvature satisfies
        \(
        R(X, T)Y = g(T, Y)X - g(X, Y)T, \quad \forall X,Y \in T(M).
        \)
        \item There exists a unit-length Killing vector field $T$ on $M$ such that every section containing $T$ has sectional curvature equal to $1$.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark} 
Let $(M,g)$ be a Sasakian manifold and $T$ the Killing vector field satisfying the above proposition.
Then the tangent bundle admits the decomposition with respect to $g$:
$$ T(M)=H \otimes V_{T }. $$
Define the $(1,1)$-tensor field $J_b=\Phi |_H$ on $H$. Then by (i) of the above proposition, it is easy to verify that $J_b^2=-\id$. Note that the complex structure $J_c$ on $(C(M),\tilde{g})$ is given by
$$ J_c(Y)=\begin{cases}
    \Phi (Y)-g(T ,Y) r \frac{\partial }{\partial r} &\text{ if }~ Y \in T(M);\\
    T  &\text{ if }~ Y=r \frac{\partial }{\partial r}.
\end{cases}  $$
Then, using the integrability of $J_c$ and the fact that $T$ is a Killing vector field, one can verify the formally integrable condition. Further analysis shows that $(M,H,J_b)$ is precisely the pseudo-Hermitian manifold with $\tau$ equal to zero.
\end{remark}

The K\"ahler metric is discussed in
Poincar\'e geometry.

\begin{remark}
This is a theorem of H\^opital.
\end{remark}
